correctness.rationale: For the specified 12 regular icosahedron vertices in six antipodal pairs, a generic central plane section has one polygon vertex for each of its 30 original edges with opposite normal signs. The six vertex axes are pairwise nonorthogonal with |cos angle|=1/sqrt5 and no three linearly dependent, hence six normal great circles have exactly 32 sign chambers. The bundled source checker makes every one of the 64 mask decisions and all 30 oriented pair-circle intersections EXACTLY in Z[sqrt5], and verifies 20 triangular chambers have 12 crossed edges and 12 pentagonal chambers have 10. I separately enumerated all 64 masks and 30 candidate crosses with geometric dot/cross operations; the category counts independently agree (the independent floating checks are corroboration; the source's symbolic sign proof establishes exhaustiveness). Each of the 30 edges is crossed by Haar normal with probability theta/pi, theta=acos(1/sqrt5); thus E[N]=30theta/pi. Since a.s. N∈{10,12}, P12=15theta/pi-5 and P10=6-15theta/pi. Independent Girard areas 20(3theta-pi)+12(2pi-5theta)=4pi agree. Nongeneric six great-circle boundaries are Haar-null; no claim about them.

originality.rationale: The six-great-circle tessellation (20 triangular/12 pentagonal spherical regions) and their spherical area fractions were previously recorded by Frederick 2023 and MathPages; both are explicitly credited. De Loera–Lopez-Campos–Torres (full arXiv HTML) study attainable slice vertex counts and the icosahedron's four-vertex gap, not Haar central-section probabilities. Jeon (full arXiv HTML) gives a distinguished equatorial decagon, not a chamber-to-polygon-type classification. Kabluchko–Seidel expected face counts are for other regular polytope families. The distinct remaining proposition is the exact incidence of every spherical sign-chamber type with 10- versus 12-gon sections and consequent complete Haar polygon-type distribution. It could be recovered quickly once incidence is known, but earlier area tables alone do not mathematically give incidence; an unindexed source might. This distinction is meaningful but narrow and priority-qualified.

value.rationale: Generic regular-icosahedron central sections form a natural finite-dimensional polytope classification problem highlighted by the icosahedral slice-gap literature. A complete exact incidence classification of all orientation chambers and the resulting genuinely nontrivial 10/12 Haar law is a standalone exact invariant of a canonical regular solid. Although the great-circle regions and their fractional areas are previously known, their verified edge-crossing correspondence is a motivated combinatorial-geometric fact rather than unmotivated enumeration.
